idea-plugin.name: SnippetVeil
idea-plugin.description:
SnippetVeil is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for anonymizing a Java snippet before it is pasted into an AI chat.

This build is a pre-release: Copy Anonymized replaces the names of project-owned types, methods, fields, parameters, locals and annotation attributes with role-preserving placeholders, and leaves JDK and third-party names untouched. A library sitting under the analysed file's own root package is treated as the company's own code and anonymized too, so that a shared internal artifact does not leak its domain vocabulary just because it arrives as a jar; the prefixes that decide this are stored per project and never synced. Package names are replaced one segment at a time — com.acme.billing becomes com.pkg1.pkg2 — so that two classes in the same package still read as being in the same package, and imports of renamed types are rewritten in place rather than dropped. A project method that overrides a JDK or library one keeps its real name — renaming it would stop it overriding, and the snippet would read as broken rather than as anonymized. A name the IDE cannot resolve is replaced as well, from an Unknown namespace of its own — so incomplete or not-yet-compiling code is covered rather than copied through. String literals are replaced as well, unless every part of one resolves to a symbol — a class name written in a string renames with the class. Comments and javadoc are stripped, and the balloon says how many were removed: prose is where a snippet's domain vocabulary actually lives, and renaming symbols does nothing to it.

Anonymize with Preview… shows the text that is about to be copied beside its mapping table before anything reaches the clipboard, and it is the only place where a name the IDE could not resolve can be released, or comments kept, for that one copy. Neither choice is remembered: a persistent setting here may only ever anonymize more.

The preview, and the read-only re-open behind the copy balloon's Show mapping, are also the only place Export Mapping… is offered. It writes that one invocation's placeholder table to a CSV file you choose — placeholder, original and kind, in first-occurrence order — so that a conversation stays decodable after the recent-history window has forgotten the locals, parameters and string literals it held. No action anywhere exports the whole stored mapping, and no action puts a mapping on the clipboard.

Settings > Tools > SnippetVeil holds the one setting that is remembered — whether libraries under this project's root package count as project code, and the package prefixes that correct it — together with the number of placeholders stored for the project and the full path of the file they are stored in, so that where the mapping lives can be checked rather than taken on trust. Reset Mappings… is there and nowhere else: it clears the mapping and the recent-history window, after a confirmation that says what that costs, and leaves the prefixes alone. No keyboard shortcut is bound by default, because every combination worth having is already taken in one keymap or another; the page links to the Keymap dialog with the action selected.

De-anonymize Clipboard is the way back: paste the AI's reply, run it from Tools > SnippetVeil or from SnippetVeil in any editor's right-click menu, and the placeholders become the real names again, on the clipboard. It is offered on every file type, because a reply gets pasted into a scratch buffer or a Markdown file rather than into .java. It matches only the exact placeholder strings this plugin minted, case-sensitively and on word boundaries, so a word the model invented is left exactly as written rather than guessed at — and the balloon says how many were restored and how many were not, split into placeholders this project has forgotten and placeholders it never issued.
